===== #447 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-03
Auto Zoom: a Back left out under one frame lets a later cut take a stale pan's aim as its base

Found by CU7's review (road map creator-jobs, Auto Zoom). It landed in commit 6ce788bf on `worktree-creator-jobs`, and was not fixed there.

**What.** In `core/src/cursor_zoom.rs`, the CU-74 loop finds the placement in force at a cut. It takes the aim of the last landed action that ends at or before the cut, and sets the later given clip's base from that aim. This is correct only while every hold ends with a Back action, because a Back's aim is `None`.

But `plan_chain` in `core/src/cursor_zoom_visits.rs` leaves a Back out when it would be shorter than one frame (`if to - from >= timing.frame`). That happens when a click lands in the last frame before a closing barrier. The barrier sets `back = bar.at - BACK`, and the Back then starts at the click (`busy`).

**Failure.** Take a run of clips continuing one source, and a click within one frame of a cut that closes the hold (for example, a cut into a given clip whose kept action meets the hold). The hold's last landed action is then the click's In or Pan, which has an aim. So that cut, or a later given cut in the same run, takes the stale aim as its clip's base: `plan_zooms` writes a `set_video` that the plan never meant, and does not close the zoom.

**Fix (the reviewer's).** Do one of these:
- Read the in-force aim only from holds that span the cut (`plan.holds`).
- Always end a closed hold with a Back marker, even a zero-length one, so that `in_force` sees `None`.

Add a `core/tests/auto_zoom.rs` case: a click within one frame of a closing cut, with a later given cut in the run. Expect no `set_video` from the stale aim.

===== #405 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
After a seek the live loudness meter counts the player's silent filler as the media at the seek's frame

Found while proving road map "audio" AP6b (the leveller), integrated in `bc885e9` on `worktree-audio-updates`.

## What happens

After `play_preview` seeks (any play not from where the stream starts), `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` hands each tap buffers whose `timeRange.duration` is zero (0/48000) and whose samples are silent (peak 0.0), but whose `timeRange.start` is the seek's frame. On a seek to 20 s: two of 4096 frames at 960000, then real audio from 963072 (logged per buffer on a Debug build, 2026-10-31).

`AudioTapContext.process` places the first of them in the live meter's ring (`meter.capture`, guarded only by a numeric time), so `LiveLoudness` sums 4096 frames of silence at [960000, 964096) and drops the overlap of what follows. Replacing those frames of the export with silence reproduces the meter's reading to four places (−23.2635 LUFS, against the export's −23.2532 over the same frames).

The first play after a build is exact, because the player's first filler carries an invalid time (`0/0`), which the capture already skips.

## How big

The error depends on the material at the seek:
- the off-mic fixture unprocessed, 12 s from 0 then 7 s from 25 s (loud speech): ΔI −0.0385 and −0.0398 LU;
- from 20 s (a quiet segment under the relative gate): 0.0000;
- levelled (the quiet segment lifted), 8 s from 20 s: −0.0102 LU on Release, −0.0041 on Debug;
- a constant pan −0.5 from 25 s (an earlier session): 0.0160.

## Tried and not kept

Not capturing a buffer whose duration is zero or invalid (a `sourced:` argument to `AudioTapContext.process`, false when `timeRange.duration` is zero or not numeric, and `guard sourced, …` before `meter.capture`) makes both seeks read 0.0000 and `audio_ap7_proof.py`'s L2 pass. But L3 (two plays of 2 s back to back, AU-72's pause and continue) then resets on the resume — "resets 4, 4, 5; from 48896 then 144511" — because the real audio resumes 5375 frames past the frame the sum reached at the pause, a gap the filler used to bridge. So the fix needs the resume path settled with it: what a resume's filler carries, and whether the frames between the sum's last tick and the pause were heard.

On the base's code the same Debug instance's `audio_ap7_proof.py` live rows read 2/4 (L2 "resets 2 -> 4", L3 "resets 5, 6, 6", one run).

## Where it shows now

AP6b's P3 (`tools/proof/audio_ap6b_proof.py`) subtracts a control — the levelled export played as a clip of its own — so the row holds the leveller's own part (spec §11 AU-67 (e)). With this fixed, the row could be absolute again.

210	Opening a project whose media was moved fails instead of offering Relink
211	
212	## Reported
213	
214	When media a project uses is moved, opening the `.reelcut` fails instead of offering a way to relink it (reported by the user, 2026-09-26).
215	
216	## What the design says should happen
217	
218	Missing media is not an open failure. `readPackage` (`app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:527`) reads only `project.json`. A clip whose file is gone draws a slate, and `EditorViewController.offerRelinkIfNeeded()` (`EditorViewController+Export.swift:117`, called from `EditorViewController.swift:296`) puts up `RelinkSheetController` ("Missing media … Locate… / Relink"). `mediaURL(for:)` (`MediaDescriptor.swift:74`) tries the stored bookmark first, then the stored path.
219	
220	## What did NOT reproduce it (build of 17ddac2, driven over MCP on a private port)
221	
222	A project with one clip of `tools/proof/media/A.mov` (a copy), saved, the instance quit, then reopened with `open_project` in a fresh instance:
223	
224	- **Case A, the file `mv`'d to another folder on the same volume:** it opens, and nothing is missing. The bookmark followed the move.
225	- **Case B, the file copied elsewhere and the original deleted:** it opens with `missing_media: [2]`, and `snapshot_ui window: sheet` shows the Missing media sheet listing `A.mov` with Locate….
226	
227	The installed `/Applications/Reelcut.app` (built 2026-09-24) already has the relink code, which dates from 2026-09-05, so an old build is not the explanation either.
228	
229	## Still to find: which condition fails
230	
231	Not tested yet. Each is a candidate:
232	
233	- The file on another volume, or on an external drive that is now unmounted. The bookmark resolves with `.withoutUI` against a missing volume.
234	- The package and its media moved together (for example a whole folder), so every absolute path is stale.
235	- Opening from Finder or File ▸ Open rather than `open_project` (NSDocumentController's own read path).
236	- A project with more than a plain clip:
237	  - a REVERSED clip. `ProjectDocument.swift:905` renders missing reversed assets behind a progress sheet, and a source that is gone may fail there;
238	  - consolidated media;
239	  - a recording;
240	  - graphics or captions;
241	  - a nest.
242	- What "fails" looked like: an alert (its text), a hang, a crash, or a window that never appears.
243	
244	## Done when
245	
246	- The failing condition is reproduced by a proof row: a project whose media is moved in that way opens, shows its slates, and offers Relink….
247	- The fix is in, and the row passes.

===== #39 [icebox] 2026-09-25
Investigate using the macos JS engine instead of quickjs

https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2

QuickJS may be performant enough to handle frames, but it doesn't support internationalization. If there's no concrete reason to prefer quickjs other than a self-contained package, the bundled js engine probably makes more sense. It *does* add some risk, as the engine version differs with os version, but JS is extremely tight on specs and implementations.


===== #110 [enhancement,needs-triage,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
Measure a wipe in the pair's union box, not each layer's own box

**A wipe between two layers of different size does not meet at one edge.** The compositor measures the wipe's edge in each layer's OWN box (spec §7.5, `designs/spec/07.5-compositor.md:77-83`), so each layer's threshold sweeps its own rectangle. Spec §7.5 calls that "the price of every nested wipe working and the common same-size pair being exact". Canvas space was considered and rejected: it breaks same-size picture-in-picture cards (a 480 px card would wipe only between p ≈ 0.70 and 0.95) and nested layers. The measure right for all cases is the PAIR's union box (and the `clip_rect` frame inside a nest), which costs uniforms and nest plumbing (effects survey E1).

Checked at `976e674`: spec §7.5 still states the per-layer measure as the accepted price; nothing measures a union box.

This is an accepted limit a later pass may revisit, not a defect. Doing it means rewriting spec §7.5's sentence, the order-of-operations comment in `Compositor.metal`, and the recipe fields that carry the box.

**Done when:** a wipe between a full-frame layer and a smaller one meets at one edge across the union box, same-size pairs and nested wipes render byte-identical to today (`tools/proof/e1_proof.py`'s wipe rows), a new row for the different-size pair is made to fail on purpose once, and spec §7.5 says the new rule.

Moved from `designs/reelcut-remaining.md` §5d on 2026-09-26. Source: `archive/reelcut-effects-survey.md` §6 (E1), §8; ADR `designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, `designs/adr/roadmap-05-transitions-motion.md`.



===== #112 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26

- Point kinds go at step 5 and `fisheye` at step 2. `mirror` is a second sample mixed by amount, not a remap.

- Output is byte-identical on one device, but GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels.

===== #125 [enhancement,spec,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-09-26
C2: a Reelcut-run relay for cloud captions, so a person needs no key

**Deferred by the user on 2026-09-21.** The product's plan is that the person supplies their own AssemblyAI key. The user deferred C2 until an integrated AI offering is designed (spec §11 R6-5's "Current product scope (2026-09-21)" note, `designs/spec/11-decisions/cloud-captions.md`).

**C2 is a relay Reelcut would run, so cloud captions work without the person holding an AssemblyAI key. It is blocked on caller identity.** A relay that spends Reelcut's AssemblyAI money must know who is calling. That needs a licence key, Sign in with Apple, an App Store receipt or a Reelcut account. None exists, and each is a road map of its own. A rate limit is not a substitute.

The designed shape (ADR `designs/adr/roadmap-06-cloud-captions.md`, "C2 — the relay"):
- **C2b, a bucket relay (recommended).**
  - The relay mints a presigned PUT, and the app uploads to the bucket directly.
  - The relay hands AssemblyAI a presigned GET, fresh at submit time and valid 24 h.
  - A webhook with a per-job secret triggers the fetch. The transcript is kept in KV for 24 h.
  - The object and the AssemblyAI transcript are deleted, and usage is metered on AssemblyAI's `audio_duration`.
  - It has no body limit and never holds the audio. R2 is the suggested bucket (no egress fee).
- **C2a, a same-protocol proxy.** It needs zero app changes (R6-6), but is limited by the host's body ceiling. That rules out AWS: API Gateway allows 10 MB and a Lambda URL 6 MB.
- **Protocol sketch:**
  - `authorization: Bearer <licence>`;
  - `POST /v1/jobs {bytes,seconds,content_type}` (401/402/413), then `PUT <upload.url>`;
  - `POST /v1/jobs/{job}/submit`, then `GET /v1/jobs/{job}`;
  - `DELETE /v1/jobs/{job}` as the acknowledgement.
- **Relay backstops:** a 24 h bucket lifecycle rule, a sweeper, idempotent submit, and never returning an AssemblyAI URL, id or error body unwrapped.
- **App side:** a `ReelcutRelayTransport`, with `CloudTranscriber` unchanged. Settings gains a Provider row and a licence field. The fake server grows the relay protocol, and proof rows 2–11 run over both transports.

Checked at `976e674`: R6-6 says a relay that must own the bytes is "one more `TranscriptTransport` conformer". **No `TranscriptTransport` protocol exists in `app/Sources`.** `CloudTranscriber` holds a concrete `AssemblyAIClient?` (`app/Sources/CloudTranscriber.swift:71`, `:84`). So C2b's first app step is introducing that seam, with `AssemblyAIClient` as its first conformer, as a pure move.

**Done when:** a caller-identity mechanism is chosen and recorded in spec §11, together with the relay decisions (C2a or C2b, metering, retention); the relay and its transport are built; and `tools/proof/cloud_captions_proof.py`'s rows 2–11 pass over both transports against the fake.

===== #131 [needs-info,ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-09-27
Opening a project whose media was moved fails instead of offering Relink

## Reported

When media a project uses is moved, opening the `.reelcut` fails instead of offering a way to relink it (reported by the user, 2026-09-26).

## What the design says should happen

Missing media is not an open failure. `readPackage` (`app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:527`) reads only `project.json`. A clip whose file is gone draws a slate, and `EditorViewController.offerRelinkIfNeeded()` (`EditorViewController+Export.swift:117`, called from `EditorViewController.swift:296`) puts up `RelinkSheetController` ("Missing media … Locate… / Relink"). `mediaURL(for:)` (`MediaDescriptor.swift:74`) tries the stored bookmark first, then the stored path.

## What did NOT reproduce it (build of 17ddac2, driven over MCP on a private port)

A project with one clip of `tools/proof/media/A.mov` (a copy), saved, the instance quit, then reopened with `open_project` in a fresh instance:

- **Case A, the file `mv`'d to another folder on the same volume:** it opens, and nothing is missing. The bookmark followed the move.
- **Case B, the file copied elsewhere and the original deleted:** it opens with `missing_media: [2]`, and `snapshot_ui window: sheet` shows the Missing media sheet listing `A.mov` with Locate….

The installed `/Applications/Reelcut.app` (built 2026-09-24) already has the relink code, which dates from 2026-09-05, so an old build is not the explanation either.

## Still to find: which condition fails

Not tested yet. Each is a candidate:

- The file on another volume, or on an external drive that is now unmounted. The bookmark resolves with `.withoutUI` against a missing volume.
- The package and its media moved together (for example a whole folder), so every absolute path is stale.
- Opening from Finder or File ▸ Open rather than `open_project` (NSDocumentController's own read path).
- A project with more than a plain clip:
  - a REVERSED clip. `ProjectDocument.swift:905` renders missing reversed assets behind a progress sheet, and a source that is gone may fail there;
  - consolidated media;
  - a recording;
  - graphics or captions;
  - a nest.
- What "fails" looked like: an alert (its text), a hang, a crash, or a window that never appears.

## Done when

- The failing condition is reproduced by a proof row: a project whose media is moved in that way opens, shows its slates, and offers Relink….
- The fix is in, and the row passes.

===== #251 [enhancement,ai-drafted,low-priority,icebox] 2026-10-07
Graphics: video input to a graphic (a video frame drawn inside a graphic's raster)

Split from #240 on 2026-10-07. The owner chose to build mattes first (#240) and to keep this half open, iceboxed, rather than close it.

**What it is.** A graphic that takes a video clip's frame as an input it can draw: a `video` prop naming a clip, which the module places with `<image>` and may clip, mask, filter, skew or tile. It is the only way to get pictures a matte cannot make — the video blurred, displaced, recoloured or warped *by* the graphic (resvg implements displacement, turbulence, colour-matrix, blur, morphology and lighting filters, on the CPU), or a frosted panel behind a lower third.

**Why it was not built with #240.** #240's research (2026-10-07) found:
- It reverses three spec §11 decisions: G-1, G-5 and, in effect, R5-1 ("effects are closed vocabularies, never a runtime").
- It puts a CPU raster of a whole video frame into every rendered frame. The engine takes only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG images, so each frame would also be encoded and decoded again. Stutter is expected at 1080p and certainly at 4K; nothing has been measured.
- It defeats the graphic texture cache and the export prefetch, for exactly the heaviest clips.
- It gives a second way to crop, round, blend and key that preview and export must keep agreeing on.
- It needs the model's first clip-to-clip reference.
- It is eight or more phases, with a spike first.

Road map 10's design had already answered "video or timeline layers as inputs to a component" with no: "Mattes are compositor features" (`designs/adr/svg-motion-plan.md:111-114`).

**What would reopen it.** The mattes from #240 proving short of a picture the owner wants, which only video inside the raster can make.

170	===== #374 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-27
171	Graphics: render SVG rasters deeper than 8 bits (supersede PR-5 for graphics)
172	
173	Graphic clips are rasterized at 8 bits per channel (spec §11 PR-5), so a smooth gradient drawn by a graphic module loses its levels before the 16-bit-float compositor ever sees it. The owner wants the bit range of SVG rasters expanded; output dithering (the 8-bit exports) is being done first as a separate change, and this issue holds the deeper part.
174	
175	## What was measured (2026-10-27)
176	
177	The promo's intro graphic draws a radial gradient from `#0D1512` to a mid green over ~800 px. Along row 540, x 0–800, of a 1920×1080 `render_frame` PNG:
178	
179	- green spans code values 23–65: 43 distinct levels, 51 steps, every step exactly one level;
180	- median flat run 14 px, widest 50 px: visible concentric rings, faintly tinted because R, G and B step at different radii.
181	
182	The same frame decoded from the H.264 export keeps 41 levels (median run 10 px, widest 56 px): the encode is not the main cause. The steps are in the raster.
183	
184	## Why it is 8-bit
185	
186	- `graphic/` renders through resvg 0.48.1 on tiny-skia 0.12.0. tiny-skia's only `Pixmap` is RGBA8.
187	- Its highp pipeline already evaluates gradients in f32, and rounds to u8 at the store stage. Its lowp pipeline (u16 fixed point) runs whenever every stage has a lowp form, as simple fills do. It has no dithering (a `// TODO` about `dither_rate` in `pipeline/blitter.rs`).
188	- resvg's filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feTurbulence`, …) operate on 8-bit buffers.
189	
190	## What expanding it would take
191	
192	1. A vendored tiny-skia patch: a 16-bit (f16 or u16) `Pixmap`, a deep store stage for highp, and forcing highp for graphics. Raster time will rise; measure it.
193	2. resvg's filters: patch them to the deep buffer, or document that a filtered region stays 8-bit.
194	3. App side: the graphic texture becomes `rgba16Float` (the compositor is already 16F, PR-1). The graphic raster cache (G-37, RAM/4 budget) holds half as many frames per byte; re-measure the budget and the prefetch (G-36).
195	4. A new spec §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics (text clips, shapes, stills and captions are PR-5's other 8-bit members; say which follow).
196	5. Proofs: graphics_proof and every frozen graphic baseline compare 8-bit pixels; they re-record or gain a deep comparison.
197	
198	Payoff: banding-free graphics in the 10-bit and ProRes deliverables, and gradients that keep their levels when a graphic is graded, faded or scaled. For 8-bit exports the output dither (done separately) is what removes the bands, so do this after it.

===== #374 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-27
Graphics: render SVG rasters deeper than 8 bits (supersede PR-5 for graphics)

Graphic clips are rasterized at 8 bits per channel (spec §11 PR-5), so a smooth gradient drawn by a graphic module loses its levels before the 16-bit-float compositor ever sees it. The owner wants the bit range of SVG rasters expanded; output dithering (the 8-bit exports) is being done first as a separate change, and this issue holds the deeper part.

## What was measured (2026-10-27)

The promo's intro graphic draws a radial gradient from `#0D1512` to a mid green over ~800 px. Along row 540, x 0–800, of a 1920×1080 `render_frame` PNG:

- green spans code values 23–65: 43 distinct levels, 51 steps, every step exactly one level;
- median flat run 14 px, widest 50 px: visible concentric rings, faintly tinted because R, G and B step at different radii.

The same frame decoded from the H.264 export keeps 41 levels (median run 10 px, widest 56 px): the encode is not the main cause. The steps are in the raster.

## Why it is 8-bit

- `graphic/` renders through resvg 0.48.1 on tiny-skia 0.12.0. tiny-skia's only `Pixmap` is RGBA8.
- Its highp pipeline already evaluates gradients in f32, and rounds to u8 at the store stage. Its lowp pipeline (u16 fixed point) runs whenever every stage has a lowp form, as simple fills do. It has no dithering (a `// TODO` about `dither_rate` in `pipeline/blitter.rs`).
- resvg's filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feTurbulence`, …) operate on 8-bit buffers.

## What expanding it would take

1. A vendored tiny-skia patch: a 16-bit (f16 or u16) `Pixmap`, a deep store stage for highp, and forcing highp for graphics. Raster time will rise; measure it.
2. resvg's filters: patch them to the deep buffer, or document that a filtered region stays 8-bit.
3. App side: the graphic texture becomes `rgba16Float` (the compositor is already 16F, PR-1). The graphic raster cache (G-37, RAM/4 budget) holds half as many frames per byte; re-measure the budget and the prefetch (G-36).
4. A new spec §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics (text clips, shapes, stills and captions are PR-5's other 8-bit members; say which follow).
5. Proofs: graphics_proof and every frozen graphic baseline compare 8-bit pixels; they re-record or gain a deep comparison.

Payoff: banding-free graphics in the 10-bit and ProRes deliverables, and gradients that keep their levels when a graphic is graded, faded or scaled. For 8-bit exports the output dither (done separately) is what removes the bands, so do this after it.



===== #379 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-28

One `av1_webm` export hung during codec export C3 (#377) and has not been reproduced.

===== #381 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-29
Import: a VP9-with-alpha WebM re-imports opaque (the BlockAdditional alpha is dropped)

Frame Job exports VP9 with alpha in WebM (`vp9_alpha_webm`, codec export C5, spec §11 CX-17), but importing that file back keeps the picture and drops the transparency.

The import rewraps a WebM into a MOV for AVFoundation (spec §11 #216-R, `ContainerRewrap*.swift`). The alpha travels as Matroska BlockAdditional ID 1, beside each VP9 frame. The rewrap copies the primary VP9 frames only, and AVFoundation's VP9 decoder has no alpha path. `vp9_alpha_export_proof.py` A12 pins today's behaviour: the copy plays, and it is opaque.

## What keeping it would take

===== #386 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-30
Speech duck: the release/attack crossing's bound ignores a next span shorter than the attack

Road map "audio" AP11 (ducking by speech, spec §11 AU-112), landed in 439c595 on `worktree-audio-updates`; left as a nit by the phase's second review.

**Where:** `core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs`, `speech_breaks` (around line 160):

```rust
let hi = e1.saturating_add(release).min(s2.saturating_add(attack)) as f64;
```

**What:** the crossing where one span's release meets the next span's attack is searched up to `s2 + attack`, taking the next span's attack line as valid all the way there. When the next span ends before that (`e2 < s2 + attack`, which needs short spans with Pre-roll and Hold near 0), the attack line is not the envelope past `e2` and the corner where the minimum changes over can be missed; the ramp across it is then interpolated between the neighbouring breakpoints instead of sampled at the corner. Only adjacent spans are paired.

**Fix:** bound `hi` by `min(e2, s2 + attack)` as well (and add a `duck_speech.rs` case with two short spans, Pre-roll and Hold 0, sampling the gain densely across the corner), or document the limit in AU-112.

Small audible effect at most: the multiplier stays between the two lines, so the duck is never deeper than Level.

===== #400 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
AP6: Enhance Voice's keep rule compares the solve against the chosen limiter, not the clip's own

Review nit from road map "audio" AP6 part 1, landed in commit 16bd934.

`app/Sources/AudioNormalize+Loudness.swift` (the keep rule, spec §11 AU-64 (f)) with `app/Sources/AudioEnhance.swift`: for Enhance Voice, `reading.limiter` is `choice.limiter`, a default `LimiterProps()` made up when the clip has no limiter. On a first press the keep rule can then fire on a clip that does not "already carry that limiter", as AU-64 (f) words it, and keep the clip's current volume. The effect stays within `keepVolumeDB` (0.05 dB) because the limiter is still written.

Fix: compare the solve's limiter against the clip's current limiter (`reading.current.limiter`) instead of the chosen one, or record in AU-64 (f) that Enhance compares against the chosen limiter.


===== #401 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31

Review nit from road map "audio" AP6 part 1, landed in commit 16bd934.

`app/Sources/ProcessedLoudness.swift`: `Memo`'s `Key` (clip id, the measurement plan's JSON, the chain) names no document. Two open projects with the same clip id, the same plan JSON (media ids, not URLs) and the same chain would share an R0, so the Volume section's At volume read-out (spec §11 AU-64 (g)) could show the other project's figure.

===== #402 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
AP6: the processed loudness render test reads only a clip's base audio, not its audio actions (AP8b)

Seen while integrating road map "audio" AP6 part 1 (commit 16bd934) after AP8b (6e1073a), which lets every audio parameter be animated as action ends.

`ProcessedLoudness.needsRender` (spec §11 AU-64 (a)) looks only at the clip's base `AudioProps`. A clip whose EQ, hum, gate, de-esser, compressor, noise reduction or isolation is set only at an action's end (base off) is planned off the loudness cache, so Loudness Normalize ignores those stages and At volume shows the cache figure with no "≈". The measurement plan (`measurementPlan`) keeps each segment's `automation` as it stands, so a rendered clip is measured through its animated stages, including a limiter set at an action's end, while R0's trial clears only the base limiter.

To decide: whether `needsRender` should also read the clip's audio actions (or the plan segment's `automation`), and how R0 treats an action-end limiter; then record it in AU-64.

===== #404 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
audio_ap6_proof.py V8: the bare -FrameJobNormalizeTargetLUFS -16 launch argument never reaches the app

Found by road map "audio" AP6c (Enhance the microphone when it lands), landed in f36ace3; the review asked for it to be filed.

`tools/proof/audio_ap6_proof.py` V8 launches its instance with `-FrameJobNormalizeTargetLUFS -16`. ===== #405 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
After a seek the live loudness meter counts the player's silent filler as the media at the seek's frame

Found while proving road map "audio" AP6b (the leveller), integrated in `bc885e9` on `worktree-audio-updates`.

## What happens

After `play_preview` seeks (any play not from where the stream starts), `MTAudioProcessingTapGetSourceAudio` hands each tap buffers whose `timeRange.duration` is zero (0/48000) and whose samples are silent (peak 0.0), but whose `timeRange.start` is the seek's frame. On a seek to 20 s: two of 4096 frames at 960000, then real audio from 963072 (logged per buffer on a Debug build, 2026-10-31).

`AudioTapContext.process` places the first of them in the live meter's ring (`meter.capture`, guarded only by a numeric time), so `LiveLoudness` sums 4096 frames of silence at [960000, 964096) and drops the overlap of what follows. Replacing those frames of the export with silence reproduces the meter's reading to four places (−23.2635 LUFS, against the export's −23.2532 over the same frames).

The first play after a build is exact, because the player's first filler carries an invalid time (`0/0`), which the capture already skips.

## How big

The error depends on the material at the seek:
- the off-mic fixture unprocessed, 12 s from 0 then 7 s from 25 s (loud speech): ΔI −0.0385 and −0.0398 LU;
- from 20 s (a quiet segment under the relative gate): 0.0000;
- levelled (the quiet segment lifted), 8 s from 20 s: −0.0102 LU on Release, −0.0041 on Debug;
- a constant pan −0.5 from 25 s (an earlier session): 0.0160.

## Tried and not kept

Not capturing a buffer whose duration is zero or invalid (a `sourced:` argument to `AudioTapContext.process`, false when `timeRange.duration` is zero or not numeric, and `guard sourced, …` before `meter.capture`) makes both seeks read 0.0000 and `audio_ap7_proof.py`'s L2 pass. But L3 (two plays of 2 s back to back, AU-72's pause and continue) then resets on the resume — "resets 4, 4, 5; from 48896 then 144511" — because the real audio resumes 5375 frames past the frame the sum reached at the pause, a gap the filler used to bridge. So the fix needs the resume path settled with it: what a resume's filler carries, and whether the frames between the sum's last tick and the pause were heard.

On the base's code the same Debug instance's `audio_ap7_proof.py` live rows read 2/4 (L2 "resets 2 -> 4", L3 "resets 5, 6, 6", one run).

## Where it shows now

AP6b's P3 (`tools/proof/audio_ap6b_proof.py`) subtracts a control — the levelled export played as a clip of its own — so the row holds the leveller's own part (spec §11 AU-67 (e)). With this fixed, the row could be absolute again.

===== #408 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
Voice isolation: no proof row shows the Status memo dropped when a render lands or fails

Found by road map "audio" AP5's second review and left (`archive/audio.md`, "AP5's record (2026-10-30)", "Review"; condensed record `designs/adr/audio.md`).

The Voice Isolation section's Status is read through `IsolationCache.Memo` (the first review's fix for a Status that decoded the plan and stat'd the media on every pane refresh, about 30 times a second in playback). The memo is held per document, clip, the two handles and the published `ReverseResolution`, and is dropped on `.reversedMediaDidChange`, which the document posts when a render lands or fails (spec §11 AU-56). Voice Effect's Status reads through the same `Memo(compute:)` (AU-146).

No row in `tools/proof/audio_ap5_proof.py` or `audio_ap5_probe.swift` holds the memo, lets a render land or fail, and reads the Status again. A memo that was never dropped would leave "Rendering…" showing after the render landed, and no row or mutant would see it.

**Done when:** a probe or instance row reads the Status before and after a render lands, and after a render fails, and a mutant that skips the memo's drop on `.reversedMediaDidChange` fails that row.



===== #409 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-10-31
IsolationRenderer: channel lanes that render different frame counts are cut to the shorter, not refused

Found by road map "audio" AP5's second review and left (`archive/audio.md`, "AP5's record (2026-10-30)", "Review"; condensed record `designs/adr/audio.md`).

`IsolationRenderer` renders each channel through its own `AVAudioEngine` manual-rendering engine in lockstep over one `RampSourceReader` (spec §11 AU-51). After each round it takes `got = min(got, Int64(lane.buffer.frameLength))` over the lanes (`app/Sources/IsolationRenderer.swift`, line 164) and writes `got` frames of each. If two lanes ever answered different counts, the longer lane's extra frames would be dropped while its engine had already moved past them, so the channels of a stereo render would drift apart with no error. Every measured render answered equal counts (AP5's P5, I1 and I6 aligned to within 0.007 samples), so this is a guard that is missing, not a defect seen.

**Done when:** a lane-count mismatch fails the render (`RenderError.failed` naming both counts, which `isolationFailed` and the Status already carry), or the extra frames are carried into the next round; a probe row or mutant drives the mismatch.

No row drives the menu to that path today (AP12's record says so after its fix pass).

===== #435 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-02
A get_media_analysis call that passes its wait cancels its job, losing up to one publish interval of work

When a `get_media_analysis` call passes `AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit` (60 s), it releases its owner, and that cancels the running job (spec §11 CJ-21). A job publishes only every 30 s and at a range's end, so whatever it analysed since its last publish is lost. Each "call again to continue" therefore keeps only what was published.

This matters for slow kinds: `masks` through the third arm on a Debug build (about half a frame a second), or long 4K windows. `shots` is fast enough not to notice.

Candidates:
- publish when the job is cancelled for a released owner;
- keep the job alive briefly past the call (a grace owner);
- publish more often for slow kinds.

Found in road map creator-jobs CO1 (landed in 33bfb571 on `worktree-creator-jobs`); see `designs/creator-jobs.md`, CO1's record ("Owed").

===== #437 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-02
Analysis reader turns every decoded frame upright, even the frames a sampled kind skips

`AnalysisFrames.read`'s direct arm (`Upright.picture(of:)`) copies every decoded frame of a rotation-tagged media into display orientation before the kind's callback sees it.

`faces` (road map creator-jobs CJ3, spec §11 CJ-33) analyses one frame in three at 30 fps, so two thirds of those copies are discarded. On a Debug build the rotated portrait fixture read at about 3 frames a second (`faces_proof.py` F3 took about 5 minutes there).

===== #438 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-02
Remove Background status: stale header summary, memoised nil stamp, analyze_cutout re-reading settled clips (CO3 review nits)

Three small problems the review of road map creator-jobs CO3 (commit af9473be, on `worktree-creator-jobs`) found and left in the code. Each was checked against that commit.

1. **The Background section's header summary stays stale while analysing.** `app/Sources/CutoutStatus+Memo.swift` (the ticker's progress-only branch, about line 158): a tick that only moves the progress refreshes the Status read-out alone (`readout.refresh()`). The section is shut by default, and its header summary, which repeats the Status words for one clip, keeps showing the first "Analyzing N %" until the state changes. 2. **A memoised nil stamp outlives Analyze Now.** `app/Sources/CutoutStatus.swift` (`stamp(media:url:cacheDir:in:)`, about line 371): the process-wide memo `stamps` stores a nil stamp too. A transient "Failed: the media file cannot be read" for the same media, URL and LUT therefore stays after Analyze Now, which clears only the pane's held status (`CutoutStatus.Memo.invalidate()`). Fix: don't memoise a nil stamp, or drop the media's entry in `ProjectDocument.analyzeMasksNow()`.

3. **`analyze_cutout` re-reads settled clips on every poll.** `app/Sources/AgentServer+Cutout.swift` (the poll loop, about line 59): each 0.25 s poll recomputes `CutoutStatus.detail(of:in:)` on main for every clip, including clips that have already settled. That is the marker read, the pack map and `subjectFound` each time, for up to 60 s. Fix: keep a settled clip's detail and re-read only the clips still analysing.

Spec §11 CO-30 and CO-31 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs-4.md`) govern all three. The record is CO3's in `designs/creator-jobs.md`.

===== #447 [ai-drafted,low-priority] 2026-11-03
Auto Zoom: a Back left out under one frame lets a later cut take a stale pan's aim as its base

Found by CU7's review (road map creator-jobs, Auto Zoom). It landed in commit 6ce788bf on `worktree-creator-jobs`, and was not fixed there.

**What.** In `core/src/cursor_zoom.rs`, the CU-74 loop finds the placement in force at a cut. It takes the aim of the last landed action that ends at or before the cut, and sets the later given clip's base from that aim. This is correct only while every hold ends with a Back action, because a Back's aim is `None`.

But `plan_chain` in `core/src/cursor_zoom_visits.rs` leaves a Back out when it would be shorter than one frame (`if to - from >= timing.frame`). That happens when a click lands in the last frame before a closing barrier. The barrier sets `back = bar.at - BACK`, and the Back then starts at the click (`busy`).

**Failure.** Take a run of clips continuing one source, and a click within one frame of a cut that closes the hold (for example, a cut into a given clip whose kept action meets the hold). The hold's last landed action is then the click's In or Pan, which has an aim. So that cut, or a later given cut in the same run, takes the stale aim as its clip's base: `plan_zooms` writes a `set_video` that the plan never meant, and does not close the zoom.

**Fix (the reviewer's).** Do one of these:
- Read the in-force aim only from holds that span the cut (`plan.holds`).
- Always end a closed hold with a Back marker, even a zero-length one, so that `in_force` sees `None`.

Add a `core/tests/auto_zoom.rs` case: a click within one frame of a closing cut, with a later given cut in the run. Expect no `set_video` from the stale aim.

133	
134	**C2 is a relay Reelcut would run, so cloud captions work without the person holding an AssemblyAI key. It is blocked on caller identity.** A relay that spends Reelcut's AssemblyAI money must know who is calling. That needs a licence key, Sign in with Apple, an App Store receipt or a Reelcut account. None exists, and each is a road map of its own. A rate limit is not a substitute.
135	
136	The designed shape (ADR `designs/adr/roadmap-06-cloud-captions.md`, "C2 — the relay"):
137	- **C2b, a bucket relay (recommended).**
138	  - The relay mints a presigned PUT, and the app uploads to the bucket directly.
139	  - The relay hands AssemblyAI a presigned GET, fresh at submit time and valid 24 h.
140	  - A webhook with a per-job secret triggers the fetch. The transcript is kept in KV for 24 h.
141	  - The object and the AssemblyAI transcript are deleted, and usage is metered on AssemblyAI's `audio_duration`.
142	  - It has no body limit and never holds the audio. R2 is the suggested bucket (no egress fee).
143	- **C2a, a same-protocol proxy.** It needs zero app changes (R6-6), but is limited by the host's body ceiling. That rules out AWS: API Gateway allows 10 MB and a Lambda URL 6 MB.

145	  - `authorization: Bearer <licence>`;
146	  - `POST /v1/jobs {bytes,seconds,content_type}` (401/402/413), then `PUT <upload.url>`;
147	  - `POST /v1/jobs/{job}/submit`, then `GET /v1/jobs/{job}`;
148	  - `DELETE /v1/jobs/{job}` as the acknowledgement.
149	- **Relay backstops:** a 24 h bucket lifecycle rule, a sweeper, idempotent submit, and never returning an AssemblyAI URL, id or error body unwrapped.

213	
214	When media a project uses is moved, opening the `.reelcut` fails instead of offering a way to relink it (reported by the user, 2026-09-26).

216	## What the design says should happen
217	
218	Missing media is not an open failure. `readPackage` (`app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:527`) reads only `project.json`. A clip whose file is gone draws a slate, and `EditorViewController.offerRelinkIfNeeded()` (`EditorViewController+Export.swift:117`, called from `EditorViewController.swift:296`) puts up `RelinkSheetController` ("Missing media … Locate… / Relink"). `mediaURL(for:)` (`MediaDescriptor.swift:74`) tries the stored bookmark first, then the stored path.
219	
220	## What did NOT reproduce it (build of 17ddac2, driven over MCP on a private port)
221	
222	A project with one clip of `tools/proof/media/A.mov` (a copy), saved, the instance quit, then reopened with `open_project` in a fresh instance:
223	
224	- **Case A, the file `mv`'d to another folder on the same volume:** it opens, and nothing is missing. The bookmark followed the move.
225	- **Case B, the file copied elsewhere and the original deleted:** it opens with `missing_media: [2]`, and `snapshot_ui window: sheet` shows the Missing media sheet listing `A.mov` with Locate….

227	The installed `/Applications/Reelcut.app` (built 2026-09-24) already has the relink code, which dates from 2026-09-05, so an old build is not the explanation either.

230	
231	Not tested yet. Each is a candidate:
232	
233	- The file on another volume, or on an external drive that is now unmounted. The bookmark resolves with `.withoutUI` against a missing volume.
234	- The package and its media moved together (for example a whole folder), so every absolute path is stale.
235	- Opening from Finder or File ▸ Open rather than `open_project` (NSDocumentController's own read path).
236	- A project with more than a plain clip:
237	  - a REVERSED clip. `ProjectDocument.swift:905` renders missing reversed assets behind a progress sheet, and a source that is gone may fail there;
238	  - consolidated media;
239	  - a recording;
240	  - graphics or captions;
241	  - a nest.
242	- What "fails" looked like: an alert (its text), a hang, a crash, or a window that never appears.

171	Graphics: render SVG rasters deeper than 8 bits (supersede PR-5 for graphics)
172	
173	Graphic clips are rasterized at 8 bits per channel (spec §11 PR-5), so a smooth gradient drawn by a graphic module loses its levels before the 16-bit-float compositor ever sees it. The owner wants the bit range of SVG rasters expanded; output dithering (the 8-bit exports) is being done first as a separate change, and this issue holds the deeper part.
174	
175	## What was measured (2026-10-27)
176	
177	The promo's intro graphic draws a radial gradient from `#0D1512` to a mid green over ~800 px. Along row 540, x 0–800, of a 1920×1080 `render_frame` PNG:
178	
179	- green spans code values 23–65: 43 distinct levels, 51 steps, every step exactly one level;
180	- median flat run 14 px, widest 50 px: visible concentric rings, faintly tinted because R, G and B step at different radii.
181	
182	The same frame decoded from the H.264 export keeps 41 levels (median run 10 px, widest 56 px): the encode is not the main cause. The steps are in the raster.
183	
184	## Why it is 8-bit
185	
186	- `graphic/` renders through resvg 0.48.1 on tiny-skia 0.12.0. tiny-skia's only `Pixmap` is RGBA8.
187	- Its highp pipeline already evaluates gradients in f32, and rounds to u8 at the store stage. Its lowp pipeline (u16 fixed point) runs whenever every stage has a lowp form, as simple fills do. It has no dithering (a `// TODO` about `dither_rate` in `pipeline/blitter.rs`).
188	- resvg's filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feTurbulence`, …) operate on 8-bit buffers.
189	
190	## What expanding it would take
191	
192	1. A vendored tiny-skia patch: a 16-bit (f16 or u16) `Pixmap`, a deep store stage for highp, and forcing highp for graphics. Raster time will rise; measure it.
193	2. resvg's filters: patch them to the deep buffer, or document that a filtered region stays 8-bit.
194	3. App side: the graphic texture becomes `rgba16Float` (the compositor is already 16F, PR-1). The graphic raster cache (G-37, RAM/4 budget) holds half as many frames per byte; re-measure the budget and the prefetch (G-36).
195	4. A new spec §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics (text clips, shapes, stills and captions are PR-5's other 8-bit members; say which follow).
196	5. Proofs: graphics_proof and every frozen graphic baseline compare 8-bit pixels; they re-record or gain a deep comparison.
197	
198	Payoff: banding-free graphics in the 10-bit and ProRes deliverables, and gradients that keep their levels when a graphic is graded, faded or scaled. For 8-bit exports the output dither (done separately) is what removes the bands, so do this after it.

389	With a clip's sound off, or a movie with no audio stream, a play or a Loop wrap in the preview sometimes stalls for seconds
390	
391	## What happens
392	
393	With a clip's sound off, or with a movie that has no audio stream, a play from paused or a Loop wrap in the preview sometimes stalls for seconds. It happened several times across five launches, never on every trial.
394	
395	This is the opposite of #520 and #537. Those holds need sound and last about half a second. This one shows up without sound and lasts seconds.
396	
397	## What was run
398	
399	Every reading below is from the built app driven over MCP, on test projects made in the app from a 5 s h264 + aac movie and a 5 s video-only movie. Each control ran 3 trials per launch, with three other lanes using the machine at the same time.
400	
401	- C1 is the 5 s movie with `set_enabled {audio: false}` on its clip. C2 is the video-only movie.
402	- D is the start deficit: a 4 s `play_preview` from paused at 0, minus the distance the player's own clock moved.
403	- The per-wrap hold comes from a 13 s Loop play with two wraps.
404	
405	Readings, in seconds:
406	
407	- **Frozen base app** (main at eab6adf2): C1 per-wrap holds [3.423, 0.086, 4.503].
408	- **Debug build of the same app code:** C1 Loop-on D [0.009, 0.008, 15.955] and per-wrap holds [0.037, 0.044, 21.565]. C2 per-wrap holds [0.395, 1.524, 4.074], with poll runs at the loop start of [0.127, 2.158] over only 15 `get_project` readings in 16 s.
409	- **Release build:** C1 Loop-on D [0.008, 20.565, 0.008] and per-wrap holds [1.500, 0.422, 0.059].
410	- **The confirm stage, frozen base app:**
411	  - Once, the first `play_preview` on C1 refused with "The preview was still seeking after 5 s, so play_preview did not start."
412	  - Once, a C1 per-wrap hold read 5.300 s.
413	
414	The other trials of the same rows read 0.008–0.09 s.
415	
416	## How to measure it
417	
418	`tools/proof/ai_docs_r2a_proof.py --only C1,C2` prints these rows as MEASURE rows. Nothing here was reproduced on purpose or looked into. The stall might come from the load on the shared machine and not from the app. A first step is to run C1 and C2 alone, on an idle machine, with more trials.

422	===== #544 [ai-drafted,low-priority,ai-docs] 2026-11-07
423	Find the rest of the preview's half-second hold when play starts, wraps or seeks with sound
424	
425	The owner chose on 2026-11-07 to keep the preview's start and seek hold for now and to look further as its own piece of work. This issue holds that investigation. It replaces #537 and #520, which measured the hold and are closed in its favour.
426	
427	## What happens
428	
429	With sound on the timeline, the preview's player holds its own clock before it moves:
430	
431	- Pressing play from paused: about 0.52–0.63 s (#537).
432	- Each Loop wrap: about 0.68–0.73 s (#520).
433	- Each seek made while playing: about 0.48–0.56 s (#520).
434	
435	With the clip's sound off, or a movie with no audio stream, the same moves hold about 0.01–0.04 s. The output device does not change it: it read the same on AirPods Max and on the built-in speakers.
436	
437	## What was run
438	
439	The built app over MCP, on test projects made from a 5 s h264 + aac movie, in ai-docs batches a1 (round 1) and r2a (round 2). `play_preview` answers the player's own `currentTime`, so the hold is wall time the player's clock did not move; a `get_project` poll at about 1 ms spacing read exactly 0 at a wrap for 0.66–0.69 s. `tools/proof/ai_docs_a1_proof.py` (W1–W7) and `tools/proof/ai_docs_r2a_proof.py` (H1–H6) print these as measurements against a 0.10 s line. `docs/manual-checks.md` PB-15 names it for a person.
440	
441	## Tried and measured (each built alone, then reverted)
442	
443	| Change | Play start (H1, Loop off) | Play start (H2, Loop on) |
444	| --- | --- | --- |
445	| The base app | 0.53 s | 0.54 s |
446	| Seeks while playing don't wait for the compositor's frame | about the same | about the same |
447	| No audio taps at all (meter dark) | — | wraps 0.28–0.45 s |
448	| S1: the ×1 track's time-pitch set to varispeed | 0.47 s | 0.45 s |
449	| S2: the item's time-pitch set to varispeed | 0.45 s | 0.45 s |
450	| S3: the metering taps moved after the effects | 0.36 s | 0.28 s |
451	| S4: preroll the player once a paused seek lands | 0.53 s | 0.52 s |
452	
453	So about half the hold comes from where the processing taps sit, the time-pitch stage accounts for under 0.1 s, and 0.2–0.4 s is unexplained. S3 would also need the level meter to learn the taps' stamps, which arrive one buffer early (#335); the owner chose not to ship it on its own.
454	
455	## Where to look next
456	
457	- `AVPlayerLooper` or an `AVQueuePlayer` for the Loop wrap.
458	- The audio mix's own render path: what the player waits for before its clock starts.
459	- An `AVSampleBufferAudioRenderer` pipeline, with S3 as the first data point.
460	
461	Done when play, a wrap and a mid-play seek with sound hold under the 0.10 s line in `ai_docs_r2a_proof.py`, with the level meter still metering (its M1 row).
462	
463	Related: #543 (with the sound off, a play or wrap sometimes stalls for seconds).

# Open issues ready to work — 2026-11-08

110 open issues on kpgalligan/framejob, each read and the claims spot-checked
against main at a0bae333. "Ready" means: the issue names the defect or the
feature precisely, names where it lives, names a fix or an acceptance, needs
no owner answer, and depends on nothing that is absent from the tree.

Every creator-jobs and audio commit the issues cite is on main. The one branch
that is not is `worktree-tutorial-handler` (e3169260), which blocks #425 and #426.

## 1. Defects with a named fix (ready, highest value per hour)

| # | What | Fix the issue names | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 447 | Auto Zoom: a Back dropped under one frame lets a later cut take a stale pan's aim as its base; writes a `set_video` the plan never meant | Read the in-force aim only from holds spanning the cut, or always end a hold with a Back marker; `core/tests/auto_zoom.rs` case | S, core |
| 456 | Switch by Speaker faces mode: empty range adds a spurious no-face refusal; a marker range past the grid forms a crossed `ClosedRange` and TRAPS (same pattern in `AnalysisMasks.swift:151`) | `count > 0` in the where clause; `guard lo <= hi`; probe rows | S, app |
| 460 | `make_vertical_version` with `path`: a failed save leaves the copy open and dirty with no `project` in the error | Close the copy, remove the package, rethrow (as `verticalCopy` does) | S, app |
| 458 | `record_screen` polish reads `document.scope` after the enhance (up to 5 min later), not at landing; a nest opened meanwhile makes every polish command drop | Read scope once in `landAndEnhance`, pass to both | S, app |
| 444 | Transcript tab keeps an old voice cache for a cloud-transcribed media until the tab is hidden and shown | One line in `cacheLanded`; `TranscriptTabSource.swift` is at 598 so a pure move first | S, app |
| 393 | Stems: with no plan the export writes only the mix but `export_status` lists stem paths that were never written | Fail the job or drop stems from the result; proof row | S, app |
| 394 | Stems: two names differing only in NFC/NFD become two stems in one file | NFC + case-fold in `export_stems.rs::same`; core test | S, core |
| 398 | `set_action_end` `off: ["audio.eq", "audio.eq.<slot>"]` silently drops the whole-EQ off | Refuse in `check_off` by sentence; `core/tests/action_off.rs`; AU-88 and §6c wording | S, core |
| 386 | Speech duck: release/attack crossing bound ignores a next span shorter than the attack | Bound `hi` by `min(e2, s2 + attack)`; test with two short spans | S, core |
| 392 | Volume line: ⌥-press in a clip's last partial frame rounds to `clip.duration`, beeps, adds no point | Floor to the frame before the guard; `volume_line_proof.py` row and mutant | S, app |
| 407 | EQ header summary reads "0 on" for an `audio.eq` with no slot on | Summarise as "off" (or store no eq) | XS, app |
| 410 | Match Audio: a refusal known only after the renders beeps twice on the menu path | Beep once; probe row counting beeps | S, app |
| 411 | Match Audio: smoothing reads a weight-0 band as 0 dB and pulls its neighbour toward 0 | Renormalise the [1,2,1] kernel at dropped bands; amend AU-125; probe row | S, app |
| 400 | Enhance Voice keep rule compares the solve against the chosen limiter, not the clip's own | Compare against `reading.current.limiter` (or amend AU-64 (f)) | XS, app |
| 401 | At-volume processed memo keyed without the document; two open projects can share a figure | Add `recipeKey` / `ObjectIdentifier` to `Key` | XS, app |
| 409 | `IsolationRenderer` lanes answering different frame counts are cut to the shorter, channels drift silently | Fail the render naming both counts; probe row or mutant | S, app |
| 397 | A voiced clip with an action-only isolation requests an isolation render it never plays (wasted render, export wait) | Leave voiced clips out of the end-driven wanted set; say so in AU-88 | S, app |
| 438 | Remove Background status: stale header summary during analysis, memoised nil stamp outliving Analyze Now, `analyze_cutout` re-reading settled clips every poll | Three one-site fixes named with line numbers | S, app |
| 406 | Normalize button tooltip in another window keeps the old mode until its section is rebuilt | Re-read `normalizeTip()` on refresh or observe defaults as `LoudnessPanelView` does; probe row | S, app |
| 459 | New Project from Range / Make Vertical fails when a thumbnail pass writes while the derived door carries caches ("could not be carried: No such file") | `DerivedCarry.copy` skips a vanished listed file (it is a cache) | S, app |
| 457 | `switch_by_speaker` parses `mute_cameras`/`apply` after planning, so a malformed value gets a plan answer first. **Part 2 (the guide sentence) is already fixed on the site**; only part 1 remains | Move argument checks before the planner | XS, app |
| 412 | Enhance Voice: the landing's follow duplicates the press's setup; `enhance_voice` reads in two main-thread hops | One shared helper; one `onMain` read | M, app |
| 413 | Leveller curve memo keyed by whole plan text, so a Target edit inside an action remakes the curves (contradicts AU-66 (e)) | Narrow the key or amend AU-66 (e); probe row counting builds | S, app |
| 435 | `get_media_analysis` past its 60 s wait cancels the job and loses up to 30 s of analysis | Publish when cancelled for a released owner (the simplest of three candidates) | S, app |
| 437 | Analysis reader turns every decoded frame upright, including the two in three `faces` discards; Debug portrait fixture at ~3 fps | Lazy upright picture; `AnalysisFrames.swift` at 409 so a pure move first | M, app |
| 369 | Audit seven other `AVAssetReader` users against #367's rule (no synchronous read on the cooperative pool); the class of hang that #367 fixed | Find each loop's thread; move to GCD or the cache lane | M, app |

## 2. Features fully specified, no owner answer needed

| # | What | Why ready | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 390 | Clip ▸ Voice ▸ submenu (16 kinds in 4 groups + None) | E8 designed it, AP14 built only the inspector section and `set_audio {voice}`, AU-146 records the menu as owed; needs validator arm, `perform_menu_item` path, `UIMenuTable` row, site menus page. The issue cites `docs/guide/`, which is retired: the site's menu reference is the target now | M |
| 541 | Spell Leveller/levelling the American way (Leveler, leveling), JSON key `leveller` unchanged | Follows #526/#538; 21 site pages, 35 `features.json` mentions, §11 quotes, pinned reasons in `audio_ap6b_probe.swift`; left out of #538 only for size | M, text |
| 434 | Find in the Transcript tab (⌘F) | Acceptance written (find bar, highlight + scroll, Return next, Esc restores keys); the owner said "later unless free" at TX2a, which is a sequencing note, not a block. TextKit 2 view so `NSTextFinderClient` over `tokenStarts`/`tokenLengths` | M |
| 387 | Voice isolation on a speed-changed, ramped or frozen clip (today plays dry, Status says so) | Two routes named (isolate the retimed audio, or retime the render through the source map); AU-55 to amend | L |
| 385 | `framejob://graphic?src=https://…` one-click import | Full shape written (CFBundleURLTypes, https-only, size cap, same import sheet showing the host); needs a §11 entry an agent can write from the issue, plus a manual-checks row. Owner "left it for later", not declined | M |
| 374 | Graphic rasters deeper than 8 bits | Owner wants it; the sequencing condition (output dither first, #375) is done. Large: vendored tiny-skia patch, filters, `rgba16Float` texture, re-measured G-37 budget, a §11 decision superseding PR-5 for graphics, baselines re-recorded | XL, spike first |

## 3. Proof, screen and spec hygiene (ready, cheap, low risk)

| # | What | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 443 | `screens.py` SECTIONS lacks `video.behind_subject` | **Already in SECTIONS (line 177). Verify `screens.py --only 11c-transcript-tab` passes P2, then close.** |
| 452 | `assistant_session_proof.py` pins `len(DEV_TOOLS) == 8` | Current line reads `len(DEV_TOOLS)` from `dev_tools` (13); check A0 passes and close, or fix the stale comment |
| 433 | `qualifier_proof.py` SHOWN anchor names a shader line that no longer exists | Confirmed: shader now `float3 grey = …` at `Compositor.metal:2645`; re-aim and run the mutant once |
| 404 | Bare `-16` launch argument never reaches UserDefaults | Both sites confirmed (`audio_ap6_proof.py:364`, `loudness_normalize_proof.py:283`); pass `<real>-16</real>`, re-run on Release |
| 440 | `co2a_proof.py` D15's BASE (f82c5b20) no longer builds against the integration core | Add `--base` or a BASE that moves with the tree |
| 388 | `ramp_proof.py` U1/P1 fail in a fresh tree (missing probe folder, missing baseline.json) | `mkdir` before the shader step; say how to make the baseline |
| 431 | `cloud_captions_probe.py` reads three tree objects not in the repository (confirmed absent) | Skip by name or pin the baseline files; state the exception to the #246 rule |
| 403 | `phase9_proof.py` detach_audio nest row disagrees since AP9's linked pair | Account for `Clip.linked` in the scoped path or the comparison |
| 454 | `phase8_chrome.py` 142/150: View menu list lacks Show Subjects; seven Media find-band checks stale since CU5/VR1 | Decide per check pane or check |
| 542 | `silence2_probe.py` section 17: a peaks or speech post no longer brings the cuts back (74/78, predates #538) | Find whether the sheet or the probe is stale; could be a real defect in Remove Silences' re-read |
| 368 | `missing_audio_proof.py` P1 has ~0.5 % margin under load | Lower floor or score against `frames_expected` |
| 396 | AP8b: no row or mutant covers skipping a segment with inert automation | Probe row + mutant |
| 408 | Voice isolation: no row shows the Status memo dropped when a render lands/fails | Probe row + mutant |
| 430 | Screen 14b skipped: needs a fixture with a cached filler transcript | Seed with `MediaTranscript.write` + `writeStamp` as `keys_probe.swift` K5p does |
| 429 | A dev hold on a package save (`-RCDevSaveHold`) so a proof can publish during one | Small; needs its §11 row, which the issue specifies |
| 446 | Spec §5.2a `video.cutout` still says "nothing draws it yet" | Confirmed at line 427; one-paragraph fix + Lines cell |
| 448 | Split `get_media_analysis` and `split_at_shots` out of §7.9e (612 lines) | `07.9h` is now taken by `07.9h-agent-switch.md`, so the new file is `07.9i`; pure move + citations |
| 424 | Spec files past ~500 lines | **Partly done**: §4.3b (364) and §7.9a (133) are already split. Remaining: `07.8-export.md` (801) and `11-decisions/audio.md` (1698) |
| 414 | Five stale texts after road map audio | Items 1–3 confirmed in code; item 4 moved to the site (`editing/insert-and-overwrite.mdx` still names only the detached sound); item 5 the 4.6 vs 4.7 LU figure is now on the site, find it there |
| 395 | Stems proof S1 can't read the Export Queue row's message | Needs `snapshot_ui` for the queue window or a result key first; lower value |

## 4. Not ready, and why

**Owner-iced (do not raise):** #39, #110, #112, #119, #124, #125, #126, #160, #192, #226, #237, #241, #251.

**Waiting on the owner for a file or a hand step:** #318, #319, #320 (camera originals), and #278 which they unblock; #131 (needs-info, PB-8 manual row); #436, #442 (S-TH1/S-RT1 fixtures; TX-19 deliberately left ends alone); #439 (S-KEY1); #453, #455 (S-PC1).

**Waiting on an owner decision:** #299 (SY-41: keep pitch left as is), #304 (both remedies tried and failed, SY-33), #383 (should GIF/APNG count against the ledger), #427 (refuse the cut vs shorten the transition: a §11 decision about what clips may do), #428 (amend CJ-24 and re-run the spike), #402 (whether `needsRender` reads actions), #380 (an LGPL-2 packaging judgment), #391 (road-map candidate), #415–#423 (tier C candidates), #441 (the spike's rule said not to build A10).

**Performance, parked by the owner ("features before performance"):** #328 and #544 (Performance project), and by nature #449 (ripple_delete_ranges 3.7 s at 4,096 clips) and #450 (timeline full draw 116 ms). #449 and #450 are well-measured and unblocked if the owner lifts that rule.

**Unreproduced or host-dependent investigations:** #379, #382 (one hang each, soak deferred by the owner; the re-run passed), #543 (stalls with sound off; first step is C1/C2 alone on an idle machine), #451 (thumbnail strip stops short on 4K fixtures, reproducible in two launches, cause unknown), #389 (meter resets on Bluetooth; needs AirPods and a chunk log), #405 (the obvious fix breaks L3's resume), #399 (limiter ceiling at ×1.5; "a guess to check first"), #370 (needs a real microphone recording and new logging), #432 (mask pack 62 MB/min; a spike with four candidate codings), #274 (needs an odd-sized camera clip; `samples/` may serve).

**Blocked on an unmerged branch:** #425, #426 (tutorials, `worktree-tutorial-handler` not on main).

**Accepted limits tracking possible work:** #381 (VP9 alpha re-import needs a decoder we don't bundle).

## Suggested first batch

Section 1 rows 447, 456, 460, 458, 444, 393, 394, 398, 386, 392 are each under an hour of code with a test the issue already names, and three of them (456's trap, 447's wrong `set_video`, 458's dropped polish) are user-visible wrong behaviour. Then 390 and 541 as the two feature-shaped items, and section 3 as a single hygiene sweep (closing 443 and probably 452 outright).

# Open issues ready to work — 2026-11-08

110 open issues on kpgalligan/framejob, each read and the claims spot-checked
against main at a0bae333. "Ready" means: the issue names the defect or the
feature precisely, names where it lives, names a fix or an acceptance, needs
no owner answer, and depends on nothing that is absent from the tree.

Every creator-jobs and audio commit the issues cite is on main. The one branch
that is not is `worktree-tutorial-handler` (e3169260), which blocks #425 and #426.

## 1. Defects with a named fix (ready, highest value per hour)

Check for `STOP:` in the spec. If present, halt (see **Stopping**).

### Stage 2 — adversary (`lc-adversary`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and only the files it names. Write 02-objections.md.`

Read the verdict line. If `verdict: proceed` and there are zero objections, copy `01-spec.md` to `03-spec-final.md` and go to Stage 3.

### Stage 1b — final design (`lc-designer`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and 02-objections.md. Write 03-spec-final.md: the revised spec plus an "Objections addressed" section.`

### Stage 3 — implement (`lc-implementer`)

Full route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read 03-spec-final.md. Implement it. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Small route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read request.md and 00-triage.md. No spec exists; implement the request directly, touching only files_likely_touched unless you justify otherwise in your notes. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Check for `STOP:` in the notes. If present, halt.

### Stage 4 — review (`lc-reviewer`)

**Skip check first.** Run `git diff --stat` (or the equivalent for the repo's VCS). If total changed lines < 80 AND `04-checks.txt` shows every verification command passing (a command recorded as `SKIPPED:` with a reason counts as passing) → skip to **Finish**.

Otherwise dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, and the git diff. Write 05-review.md.`

If `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If `verdict: fix-required` → Stage 5.

### Stage 5 — fix loop (`lc-fixer`, then `lc-reviewer`), at most 5 passes

Fix pass `N` runs from 1 to 5. The review it answers is `05-review.md` for pass 1, and `07-review-N.md` (the re-review written after pass `N-1`) after that.

1. Fix dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read <that review> and the git diff. Fix every blocker and should-fix. Re-run the spec's verification commands that your fixes can affect. Write 06-fix-notes-N.md.`
2. If the fix notes contain `STOP:`, halt (see **Stopping**).
3. Re-review dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, every 06-fix-notes-*.md so far, the review pass N answered, and the git diff. Write 07-review-<N+1>.md.`
4. If that review says `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If it says `fix-required` and `N < 5` → run pass `N+1`. If `N = 5` → do NOT run the fixer again. Go to **Finish** and report the unresolved findings.

**Stop early** if a re-review lists a blocker or should-fix that the previous review also raised (the same finding at the same file:line) and the fix notes claim it fixed. Go to **Finish** and report that finding as stuck. A sixth pass won't fix what two passes couldn't.

## Stopping

Any stage may write `STOP: <reason>` at the top of its output file. When you see it: halt, tell the user the reason, list the handoff files that exist, and ask how to proceed. Do not try to work around it yourself.

## Resume

List `$HANDOFF`. Restart from the first stage whose output file is missing, following the same routing rules. If `00-triage.md` says `small`, the missing spec files are expected — go by the small route. In the fix loop, the pass number is one more than the count of `06-fix-notes-*.md` already written. If the newest file is a fix note with no `07-review-*.md` after it, run that pass's re-review first. A handoff dir from before the loop (`06-fix-notes.md`, `07-review-2.md`) counts as pass 1.

## Finish

Print a summary, in this order, nothing extra:

- Route: small / full
- Stages run (including how many fix passes)
- Files changed (from `git diff --stat`)
- Verification: pass / fail, with the failing command names if any
- Objections the designer declined (from `03-spec-final.md`), one line each, if any
- Unresolved review findings (blockers / should-fix), if any
- Handoff dir path

## Rules you must not break

- One agent at a time. Sequential only.
- No agent outside the six defined. No ad-hoc "let me just check" subagents.
- Never skip triage.
- Never run more than 5 fix passes, and never run a fix pass without a `fix-required` review in front of it.
- Never paste handoff file contents into dispatch prompts — pass paths.
- You do not read source files. If you're tempted to, you're doing the designer's job at the wrong effort level.

name: parallel-worktree-lanes
description: Owner 2026-10-25 — run independent issues in parallel worktree lanes like ~/devel/rasterize, one orchestrator integrating onto main one at a time
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The owner asked on 2026-10-25, during the dedup queue: "Run changes in multiple worktree lanes, similar to how ~/devel/rasterize works on multiple tasks". Rasterize runs three lanes (a, b, c), each a worktree on its own branch. Each lane runs one batch at a time through litecode, and a single controller rebases each finished batch onto main, re-gates it and fast-forwards main. Nothing is pushed.

**Why:** throughput. Running issues one at a time leaves the machine (12 cores, 96 GB) idle.

**How to apply:**
- Put lane worktrees outside the repo: `~/devel/framejob-lane-<x>`. CoW-copy `tools/proof/media`, `agent/node_modules` and `tools/proof/work` into each with `cp -cR`. Run `make rust` in each before the first gate, so a cold build doesn't hit the 600 s cap.
- Split lanes by area so their files don't overlap.
- Run the lanes as one Workflow: issues within a lane run in sequence, and integration is serialized behind a JS mutex.
- Keep three lanes at most. Disk is tight: about 55 GB free, and each lane needs about 6 GB of build products.
- Main stays clean and is only ever fast-forwarded.
