presses its own Follow once it is first enabled (spec §11 VR-29 (h)); and
`-RCDevVerticalAccept YES` (or `in-place`, which unticks Make a copy first),
with which the Make Vertical Version sheet presses its own Make once it is
first enabled (spec §11 VR-39 (h)); and `-RCDevDerivedHidden YES`, with which `new_project_from_range` opens its
document with no window (`display: false`), so a proof can see the windowless
door (spec §11 CJ-52); and `-RCDevVerticalSaveFault <name>`, with which
`make_vertical_version`'s save to a `path` whose last component is `<name>` fails,
so a proof can see the copy closed and its package removed (spec §11 #460); and
`-RCDevExportFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`, the same for an
`ExportWriter` export's pumps, spec §11 #378), which
Distribution does not. `rc_op_names`
and the catalog are the authority for the counts; the parity check compares
them at startup. `render_frame` writes a PNG and returns its path; `export`
puts the job on the Export Queue and answers an `export_id` at once, and
`export_status` answers it until `done` (`mcp.py`'s `export_with` waits; spec
§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. Its scale is
`-RCDevCaptureScale 1|2|3` (spec §11 #539), which `screens.py` pins to 2, so a
capture is 2× on a 1× display without moving a window. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

**What was run.** On a Debug build, `land_recording {door: "panel", enhance: true, movie, cursor, voice: [a 20 s spoken m4a made with `say -v Samantha`]}` into a saved package (`cu10_proof.py`'s fixture, 640 × 360, 30 fps) ends its Enhance follow-up with no "Enhance Voice" undo step — with or without `auto_zoom`, and with no nest open. The same files through the tool door (`land_recording` without `door`) answer an `enhance` object (renders 2, result −16.0 LUFS) and step "Enhance Voice". With no `follow_wait` and 40 s of polling `perform_menu_item`'s `window.sheet`, no Measuring Sound sheet was ever up.

**What shows it is Debug's.** `audio_ap6c_proof.py` V4 (a voice-over of the owner's RØDE file, `-RCDevRampRenderHold 3`) does see the sheet and the step, and on Release `cu10_proof.py` P5 (the same fixture, a nest opened during the wait) stepped "Enhance Voice" too: its undo read "Auto Zoom", "Enhance Voice", "Add Recording". So the gap is Debug-only (timing, or a Debug-only path).

**What is in the tree now.** `cu10_proof.py` P5 requires "Auto Zoom" then "Add Recording" with "Enhance Voice" allowed but not required between them (`NESTED_STEPS`), so it no longer shows end to end that the panel door's Enhance survives a nest on every build; only `cu10_probe.py` Q7 (helper level) covers the Enhance half of #458's panel door. The review of batch c1 noted this as its one nit.

**To do.** Find which `RecordingEnhance.tick` arm ends the follow on Debug (`.drop`, or `.enhance` then a refusal at the inspector's foot) and fix it if it is an app defect; otherwise pin P5's Enhance half `release_only` with the reason (spec §11 V-4). Then make `cu10_proof.py` P5 require the three-step list "Auto Zoom", "Enhance Voice", "Add Recording".

class Doc:

    def __init__(self, client, name):
        self.client = client

        if self.path.exists():

        client.call("new_project", path=str(self.path))

        return self.client.call_with(tool, {"project": str(self.path), **arguments})

        return self.call("get_project")["project"]

    def undo_names(self, n):
        return [self.call("undo").get("undone") for _ in range(n)]

        try:

        except mcp.ToolError:

**It is not a Debug-only path, and it is not Enhance alone. Auto Zoom's follow runs in a gap at the end of the Measuring Sound sheet and makes Enhance's answer stale.**

What was run:
- `land_recording {door: "panel", enhance: true}` with no polish: the voice clip's audio changed 5.6 s after the landing and undo read "Enhance Voice", "Add Recording". Twice. So the panel door's Enhance does step on Debug.

  - 16:22:55.850 the sheet presented, `attachedSheet` set at once;
  - 16:22:58.608 the polish follow ran Auto Zoom, reading `RecordingEnhance.isPending` false and `attachedSheet` nil;
  - 16:22:58.629 the measurement's hand-back, `stale` true.

Why: `RecordingEnhance.tick` ends its follow before it shows anything, so `isPending` is false for the whole measurement, and the polish follow's only other guard is `window.attachedSheet != nil` (`RecordingPolish+Follow.swift`, `tick`). `AudioMeasureSheetController` dismisses itself when the outcome arrives and delivers the outcome on the main queue's next turn after `viewDidDisappear`. Nothing in that sequence is Debug's; Release has the same gap and a 0.5 s timer either lands in it or does not, so a Release pass is luck with the timing, not a different path.

The "without auto_zoom" report in this issue did not reproduce. A likely cause: `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` returns when the follow ENDS, which is about 2.7 s before the step lands (the measurement runs after it). A run with `follow_wait: 90` came back in 3 s with `enhance_pending: false`; reading undo straight away found only "Add Recording", and that undo is itself an edit that makes the measurement stale.

Fix candidates:
1. `RecordingEnhance` keeps a per-document "measuring" state from `.enhance` until `enhanceLanded`'s answer or refusal lands, and the polish follow's `enhancing` (and CU-101 (a)'s clock restart) reads it. `isPending` can stay as documented.
2. `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` (and `enhance_pending`) also wait on that state, so a proof reads after the step.
3. Then `cu10_proof.py` P5 requires all three steps on every build, as this issue's "To do" says, with a mutant that drops the new state.
EOF

content.text:
Both are diagnosed, and neither is fixed yet. The diagnoses are recorded as comments on the issues, and the tree is clean.

## #546: Enhance Voice makes no step on a Debug build

This is not Debug-only, and Enhance on its own is fine. The step is lost only when Auto Zoom is also asked: its follow-up commits in a short gap at the end of the Measuring Sound sheet, which makes Enhance's answer stale.

- **Enhance alone works on Debug.** With the issue's fixture and the panel door, the voice clip was enhanced 5.6 s after landing and undo read "Enhance Voice", "Add Recording". This happened twice.
- **With Auto Zoom, Enhance is lost.** Undo read only "Auto Zoom", "Add Recording", twice.
- **The cause, seen with temporary logging (reverted).** The Enhance follow marks itself finished before the measurement starts, so the only thing holding Auto Zoom back is the sheet on the window. The sheet dismisses itself and hands back its result one main-queue turn later. In that gap the Auto Zoom timer fired, saw no sheet, and committed. The hand-back arrived 21 ms later, found the project changed, and refused with "Choose Enhance Voice again."
- **Release has the same gap.** A 0.5 s timer either lands in it or does not, so the Release pass was timing luck, not a different path.
- **The "without Auto Zoom" report did not reproduce.** The likely cause is in the dev tool: `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` returns about 2.7 s before the step lands. Reading undo straight away finds no step, and that undo itself makes the measurement stale. I reproduced exactly that.

The fix I'd make: Enhance keeps a per-document "measuring" state until its answer lands, and the polish follow and `follow_wait` both wait on it. Then `cu10_proof.py` P5 can require all three steps on every build.

## #547: stale mutant anchor in `shot_split_proof.py`

The anchored line was moved, not rewritten. The CO1 commit (33bfb571) moved it byte for byte into `AnalysisClipTimes.swift`, where it occurs exactly once. The fix is one path in the proof's `mirror-skipped` row, then one mutant run to see S2 fail under it.

Say the word and I'll apply both fixes directly.

input.description: Fix #546 Enhance/polish race
input.prompt:
Work in /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob (branch main). The tree has ONE uncommitted change that is not yours and must stay: `tools/proof/shot_split_proof.py` (issue #547's fix). Fix GitHub issue #546: read it with `gh issue view 546 --comments`; the last comment is the diagnosis and it is measured, not a guess. Read `app/CLAUDE.md` before writing Swift.

## The defect

When a recording lands through the recorder panel with both "Enhance the microphone when it lands" and a polish command (e.g. Auto Zoom), Enhance Voice's step is lost. `RecordingEnhance.tick` (`app/Sources/RecordingEnhance.swift`) ends its follow BEFORE calling `AudioMeasureDoor.enhanceLanded`, so `RecordingEnhance.isPending` is false for the whole measurement. The polish follow (`app/Sources/RecordingPolish+Follow.swift`, `tick`) is then held only by `window.attachedSheet != nil`. `AudioMeasureSheetController` dismisses itself and delivers the outcome one main-queue turn after `viewDidDisappear`; in that gap the polish timer fires, commits Auto Zoom, and `AudioMeasureDoor.measure`'s stale test refuses Enhance ("Choose Enhance Voice again."). Measured on Debug: polish ran 21 ms before the hand-back. Not Debug-only; Release has the same gap.

Second, the dev tool `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` and `enhance_pending` (`app/Sources/AgentServer+LandRecording.swift`, `landThroughPanel`) read `isPending`, so they report done ~2.7 s before the step lands.

## The fix to build

1. `RecordingEnhance` keeps a per-document "measuring" state from the `.enhance` step until `enhanceLanded`'s answer OR any refusal/cancel has landed (every exit of `AudioMeasureDoor.enhanceLanded` and `measure` for that call: the early refusals, the no-render path, the sheet's hand-back, the sheet's Cancel, the document going away). Keep `isPending`'s documented meaning (the timer) unless changing it is cleaner; the type doc says "The follow ends before anything is shown" and "`isPending` never depends on the sheet" — respect or deliberately amend that doc. A leaked state would hold the polish forever, so make leaking impossible by construction (e.g. a completion closure `measure` always calls exactly once, including on Cancel; check `AudioMeasureSheetController`'s cancel path, which today calls nothing back).
2. The polish follow's `enhancing` (and CU-101 (a)'s clock restart when Enhance ends) reads the timer-pending OR measuring state.
3. `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` loop and `enhance_pending` include the measuring state. Update the tool's description text if what it says changes.
4. Check the tool door (`AgentServer.landAndEnhance` / `polishLanded`) for the same class of gap; it is believed sequential and unaffected. Say what you found.
5. Spec: the decisions are §11 AU-68 (Enhance on landing) and CU-101 (the polish), in `designs/spec/11-decisions/` (find the files with grep; never read the spec whole). Amend in place, citing #546, in the style of the nearby "#458" amendments; update Lines cells if counts change (`python3 tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`). Update the doc comments of the types you change. If `app/CLAUDE.md`'s map entry for a file you changed no longer describes it, do NOT edit CLAUDE.md: list the exact edit under "CLAUDE.md edits owed" in your report.
6. File size: a file at ~600 lines must give something up first as a pure move; check `wc -l` of each file you grow.

## Proof

- `tools/proof/cu10_proof.py` row P5: make it require exactly "Auto Zoom", "Enhance Voice", "Add Recording" (drop the two-step alternative in `NESTED_STEPS` and rewrite the docstring paragraph that excuses Debug). Consider also a plain row or extend P1b so the no-nest Enhance + Auto Zoom order is covered with `follow_wait` (undo must read Auto Zoom, Enhance Voice, Add Recording and `enhance_pending` false only after the step). `cu10_probe.py` exists for helper-level rows if useful.
- Add a mutant to `cu10_proof.py`'s `MUTANTS` that removes the new holding (polish no longer reads the measuring state); it must be CAUGHT by P5 or your new row. Because the race is timing-dependent (21 ms window against a 0.5 s timer), the mutant may not fail every run: if so, build a deterministic seam instead of relying on luck (for example a probe row asserting the polish's `decide` input `enhancing` is true while measuring, or a dev-only launch default holding the hand-back; a new dev default needs a line in the root CLAUDE.md's list, which you report as owed, and its §11 row). Prefer the simplest deterministic check.
- Run: `make typecheck` (0 errors, exactly 4 baseline warnings), `make app-debug`, the changed rows on Debug, the mutant once, then `make gate` once in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000; if it passes the cap re-run it, it skips what passed), then `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/cu10_proof.py` whole once, and `audio_ap6c_proof.py` on Release (it covers Enhance on landing; read its header for how to run it). Record each command and result.

## Rules

Do not commit or push. Never edit any CLAUDE.md. Never read anything under `.secrets/`; no paid or `--live` runs. Never take the Mac's focus (no `open`, no osascript, no posted events). Never perform a persisting menu item. Kill only a Frame Job pid you launched; another session's instance may be running. Scratch files go in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevingalligan-devel-framejob/e69fe0e8-defd-4d3d-ae59-a1fd582b8091/scratchpad/i546fix/. If the fix needs a product decision the owner would notice, stop and report the question instead of choosing.

## Report (under 350 words)

What you changed per file, the tool-door finding, each verification command with its result (the mutant's CAUGHT line, gate PASS line, Release scores), `git status --porcelain`, CLAUDE.md edits owed with exact text, and anything unresolved.

Both fixes are implemented and verified in the working tree. Nothing is committed, and both issues are still open.

**#547, the stale mutant anchor.** One path changed in `shot_split_proof.py`. The `mirror-skipped` mutant now applies and is caught: S2 fails on the reversed placement only, which is the decision that mutant breaks.

**#546, Enhance Voice lost when a polish command follows it.**
- **The fix.** Enhance now counts a per-document "measuring" state from the moment it decides to enhance until its answer, refusal or Cancel has landed. The polish follow and `land_recording`'s `follow_wait` both wait on it. The state releases itself if dropped, so it cannot hold the polish forever.
- **A second gap, same class.** `record_screen`'s polish also checked only the timer when a panel landing's Enhance was measuring in the same document. It now waits too.
- **Cancel now reports back.** The Measuring Sound sheet used to call nothing on Cancel; it now calls a `stopped` callback, so the state always ends.
- **Deterministic proof.** A new dev-only launch default, `-RCDevMeasureHandBackHold`, holds the sheet's hand-back so the 21 ms gap becomes two seconds. New rows P6 and P7 in `cu10_proof.py` use it, and P5 now requires all three steps on every build.
- **One change you didn't ask for.** `audio_ap6c_proof.py` V4 relied on `follow_wait` returning mid-measurement, so it failed on the first Release run (36/39). The subagent reworked the row to poll for the sheet instead; it now passes.

| `cu10_proof.py` on Release | 9/9 |
| `audio_ap6c_proof.py` on Release | 39/39 |
